artworks.title: Medea Rejuvenates Aeson
artworks.description: Guidobono paints Ovid's miracle: Medea restores Jason's aged father Aeson with her cauldron-brew — the Iolcan king made young again while Pelias still waits for the same gift.

artworks.title: Medea Rejuvenating Aeson
artworks.description: Giaquinto's Metropolitan Museum canvas stages the Metamorphoses scene: Aeson on the couch as Medea's herbs reverse years — the rightful king of Iolcus briefly returned to youth.

artworks.title: Medea Rejuvenating Eson
artworks.description: Dutch cabinet painting of Medea's laboratory: Aeson (Eson) as the patient of Colchian magic — the father for whose throne Jason sailed, restored before the Pelias daughters ask for the same rite.

artworks.title: Medea Draining the Blood of Aeson
artworks.description: Wellcome Collection engraving of the grisly first step: Medea drains Aeson's blood to refill him with her brew — Ovid's surgery made into a print of medical wonder and mythic horror.

artworks.title: Medea Cooking Magical Herbs for Aeson
artworks.description: Mannerist engraving from the Histoire de Jason: Medea tends the cauldron that will renew Aeson — the print series that taught Europe Jason's father as the first beneficiary of Colchian arts.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Ovid gives Aeson the full rejuvenation episode (Book 7): Medea's herbs, the drained veins, and the king of Iolcus made young — the scene painters never tired of.

popCulture.title: Aeson
popCulture.description: Son of Cretheus, father of Jason, rightful king of Iolcus until Pelias usurped the throne — restored to youth by Medea in Ovid's telling.
